_doc: Performance budgets as code — machine-independent latency SLOs. A budget is the maximum allowed ratio of a benchmark's median to the calibration anchor's median (calibration/anchor). Because both are measured on the same host, the ratio cancels machine speed: a budget of 5.0 means 'no slower than 5x this machine's calibration workload', and holds on any runner. `bench-tools budget` fails (exit 1) on any breach. These are EVIDENCE-CALIBRATED from a full breed_latency run (calibration ~17.8us): the bulk of breeds measure 0.4-6.5x calibration, so default 15.0 gives ~2x headroom; rl_symbolic (Q-learning convergence) is the lone outlier at ~64x and gets a 100x ceiling. Tighten as longer, less noisy runs accumulate.
